title: The 80% Draft: Why Context Matters More Than the Model in Financial Services Marketing
summary: A draft generated in seconds can still take hours to approve. See how persistent brand context helps financial services teams produce AI content that needs less rewriting and fewer rounds of review.
body_markdown:
**In short**


AI content quality in financial services depends on how well each draft reflects the firm's brand voice, approved claims, disclosures, and audience. An "80% draft" starts close to approval, reducing the rewriting and compliance rework that slow content production. Persistent, governed context helps marketing teams produce more consistent drafts and improve them over time.


Every financial services marketing team that has tried AI knows the moment. A draft appears in seconds. Then someone spends an hour fixing it.


The tone is close but not quite the firm's. A product feature is described in a way compliance never approved. The disclosure is missing, or it's last year's version. A line or two reads so obviously machine-written that a reviewer flags it before getting to the substance.


Getting to a first draft was never the real bottleneck. What matters is how far that draft is from something a reviewer can approve.


The goal is an 80% draft: a first version that already reflects the firm's voice, approved claims, disclosures, and audience, so the remaining work is judgment and polish. Getting there reliably depends far less on the AI model than on the context behind it.


## Key takeaways


- AI content quality in financial services depends on grounding drafts in the firm's brand voice, product knowledge, approved claims, and compliance requirements.
- Persistent, governed context helps teams produce more consistent drafts without rebuilding instructions for every request.
- Tracking revision rounds, approval time, and recurring compliance feedback reveals whether AI is improving content production.
- Jasper IQ provides a shared foundation for applying brand guidelines, audience knowledge, product information, and marketing best practices across AI workflows.


## Why AI-generated content gets stuck in financial services compliance review


General AI tools are capable, but they know nothing about your firm. Without persistent, governed context, each new session depends on whatever information a marketer provides.


In financial services, that gap is expensive. A draft missing the right context creates three kinds of rework:


- **Voice rework.** The content doesn't sound like the firm, so an editor rewrites it.
- **Accuracy rework.** Product details, rates, or claims drift from what's approved, so someone checks every line against source material.
- **Compliance rework.** Disclosures are missing or misplaced, or the overall message promises more than it should, so the piece comes back from review.


Compliance rework can be especially costly, because every returned draft restarts the review cycle. A[governance-first approach](https://www.jasper.ai/blog/governance-first-financial-services-marketing) to AI content creation can help financial services teams reduce recurring compliance issues and avoid unnecessary review cycles.


## What is AI context infrastructure for financial services marketing?


Context infrastructure is the persistent, governed knowledge an AI system draws on every time it creates something. Rather than living in individual prompts, it's built once, maintained centrally, and applied across drafts.


For a financial services marketing team, that includes:


- **Brand voice** , defined by examples and rules, so drafts sound like the firm.
- **Style guidelines** , including preferred terms, phrases to avoid, and the patterns that make copy read as AI-written.
- **Audiences** , covering the needs and sensitivities of retail customers, high-net-worth clients, advisors, and institutional investors.
- **Product and company knowledge** , including approved claims, current rates and figures, and the disclosures each product requires.
- **Marketing best practices** , so structure and format fit each channel.


At Jasper, this layer is[Jasper IQ](https://www.jasper.ai/jasper-iq) . It serves as a shared foundation for marketing context, bringing together the knowledge and standards that make content specific to a firm and applying them across agents and workflows.


Integrations and MCP extend access to that context into other systems teams use, helping maintain consistent brand standards beyond a single tool.


## How better AI context improves content quality over time


When context lives in prompts, quality depends on who wrote the prompt. The most experienced marketer on the team gets strong results. A new hire or a regional team gets something different. Every improvement stays local and temporary.


When context lives in shared infrastructure, improvements can be applied across the team. Compliance clears new disclosure language once, and the approved version can inform future drafts. A reviewer flags a phrase that keeps causing trouble, it goes into the style guidelines, and teams can prevent the same mistake from recurring.


The system gets better with use, and the whole team benefits.


Performance data closes the loop. When you can see which pages get cited in AI answers, which variants convert, and which drafts clear review on the first pass, you can feed those insights back into the context the system uses next time.


## How higher-quality AI drafts improve financial services marketing workflows


When drafts arrive at 80%, the work itself shifts.


**Editors edit.** Time moves from rewriting to refining: sharpening an argument, choosing a better example, tightening a headline.


**Reviewers review.** Compliance attention goes to the judgment calls that need an expert, instead of repeatedly catching missing disclaimers.


**Performance follows.** At U.S. Bank, John Dotto, SVP of Digital Marketing, has said, "Jasper was outperforming 75% of our human-generated content." Akbank saw a 40% reduction in time spent creating content for personalized push and SMS campaigns aligned to its brand voice.


**Scale becomes realistic.** One campaign concept can become hundreds of assets across segments, languages, and channels, as long as each starts from the same governed context.


With that foundation in place, always-on agents can take ownership of defined areas of work, like keeping product content current or building content for AI search, while people retain responsibility for decisions that require human judgment.


## How to build AI context infrastructure for financial services marketing


Building context infrastructure is less work than most teams expect, because much of the material already exists in brand guidelines, persona decks, approved claims libraries, and past compliance feedback.


The fastest way to build it is around a real piece of work rather than as a standalone setup project.


At Jasper, our[forward-deployed teams](https://www.jasper.ai/blog/inside-jaspers-forward-deployed-services-model) help customers build this foundation alongside their existing marketing processes. This hands-on expertise is one of the key capabilities financial services teams need from an[AI content platform](https://www.jasper.ai/blog/financial-services-teams-ai-content-platform) . At Jasper, our forward-deployed teams do this alongside customers. AI search is often the first workflow, because it shows exactly how the brand is represented today and where the context is thin.


A practical sequence:


1. **Pick one workflow that matters.** Identify a high-value use case and agree on the quality, accuracy, and review requirements the output must meet.
2. **Gather what you have.** Bring together brand guidelines, voice examples, persona documents, product sheets, and approved disclosure language.
3. **Bring it into the system.** Set up brand voice, style guidelines, audiences, and knowledge, and connect the tools the workflow touches.
4. **Decide where people stay in the loop.** Establish who reviews what, which decisions require human judgment, and[where approval happens](https://www.jasper.ai/blog/where-jasper-fits-in-financial-services-marketing) .
5. **Run it, measure it, and feed review back in.** Compare revision rounds against your baseline, and turn recurring reviewer comments into updated guidelines.
6. **Extend the same foundation.** Apply the context to campaigns, personalization, translation, and the next workflow.


The result is a foundation teams can build on without recreating the same knowledge and governance requirements for every new use case.


## How to measure AI content quality and approval efficiency


Speed to first draft is the wrong headline metric. A draft generated in seconds offers little value if it takes hours to correct or repeatedly fails compliance review.


Better metrics to track include:


- **Revision rounds per asset before approval:** How often does a draft need to be rewritten or returned?
- **Time from first draft to approval:** How long does content spend in editing and review?
- **Share of drafts approved with only minor edits:** How often does the first version meet the team's quality standards?
- **Recurring review comments:** Are the same brand, accuracy, or compliance issues appearing less frequently over time?


Establish a baseline before introducing governed AI workflows, then compare results across similar asset types.


If revision rounds decline and more drafts reach approval with minor edits, that's evidence the context is improving output quality.


## Build AI content that's closer to approval from the first draft


AI models will keep improving, and a system that works across them lets you take advantage of each one. What makes the output yours, and approvable, is the context behind it.


Build that well once, and every draft after it starts most of the way there.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How can financial services marketers improve AI content quality?


Financial services marketers can improve AI content quality by grounding generation in persistent, governed context that includes brand voice, approved product claims, required disclosures, and audience information. Shared context helps AI produce more consistent drafts and reduces the manual rewriting needed before review.


### Why do AI-generated drafts struggle with financial services compliance review?


AI-generated drafts often struggle with compliance review because they lack access to a firm's approved claims, current product information, and disclosure requirements. Without that context, content may contain inaccurate statements or unsupported messaging that requires correction before approval. Human compliance review remains necessary.


### What is an 80% draft in AI content creation?


An 80% draft is a first version of content that already reflects most of the firm's brand, factual, audience, and compliance requirements. The term describes a quality goal rather than a fixed approval score. The objective is to reduce extensive rewriting so editors and reviewers can focus on refinement and judgment.


### How does Jasper IQ improve AI content quality for financial services?


Jasper IQ provides a persistent intelligence layer that applies brand voice, style guidelines, audience information, and approved company and product knowledge across content creation workflows. This helps financial services teams generate content grounded in their firm's established standards, reducing inconsistencies and repeated manual corrections.


### How should financial services teams measure the quality of AI-generated content?


Teams should measure revision rounds, time from first draft to approval, the percentage of drafts requiring only minor edits, and recurring compliance feedback. These metrics help determine whether AI is reducing review effort and improving the consistency of content that reaches approval.
